column3: NASB renders “differs in nothing” as “does not differ at all” and adds “although.”
NASB renders “trustees” as “managers” and “the time appointed” as “the date set.”
NASB follows the critical text; “basic principles” is rendered “elemental things.”

NASB follows the critical text (“through God”) without the Textus Receptus “of God through Christ”; it adds “then.”
NASB adds “when” and renders “were enslaved to” as “were slaves to.”
NASB renders “destitute” as “worthless,” “principles” as “elemental things,” and “anew” as “all over again.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “toiled for” as “labored over.”
NASB moves “I beg of you, brethren” to the front and ends the verse with a semicolon.
NASB renders “in weakness of the flesh” as “because of a bodily illness” and “at the first” as “the first time.”
NASB follows the critical text (“your trial”); it renders “in my flesh” as “in my bodily condition” and “reject with contempt” as “loathe,” and adds “Himself.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Where”); “blessedness” is rendered “sense of blessing.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “are zealous after” as “eagerly seek,” “not rightly” as “not commendably,” and “exclude” as “shut … out.”
NASB follows the critical text; “to be zealous” is rendered “to be eagerly sought.”
NASB follows the critical text (“children,” “until”); “travail” is rendered “am … in labor,” and the verse ends with a dash.
NASB renders “I was wishing” as “I could wish.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “the slave woman” as “the bondwoman.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “son” and renders “slave woman” as “bondwoman.”

NASB follows the critical text; it renders “are allegorized” as “This is allegorically speaking,” adds “women,” and renders “begetting unto slavery” as “bearing children who are to be slaves.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text (“Now … for”); it adds “this.”
